evidence:
Authored for this product: instruction.md:1 frames a specific recruiting team ('the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day') with two coupled surfaces - a per-job pipeline board and per-application recruiter-candidate conversations - and a concurrency theme ('nobody's work gets trampled'). hireops_rules.md is product-specific throughout: four roles incl. Observer and Candidate (s1), six stages with Rejected-from memory and reopen-to-origin (s3), hand-set shared intra-stage order, per-job interview places, hiring-manager late-stage scope, 409 with 'by whom', optimistic-move rollback keeping focus, all-or-none bulk moves in board order, single-level undo with touch invalidation (s3 Undo lines 94-100), activity lines (s4), 15-second live updates preserving typing/focus/scroll (s5), 30-message paging with anchored scroll, per-person unread, seen rules excluding the observer, per-user per-browser drafts surviving session expiry (s6), and candidate wording table plus data-exclusion list (s7). The 43 functional criteria (hro_* ids, judge.toml lines 23-402) map onto these product promises. task.toml name/description/keywords/arena_slice/difficulty_explanation all describe this recruiting product. Grep of the frozen task for sibling nouns (pellmoor, threadline, bazaar, torque, vacancy) found none; 'panel' appears only in seed message filler text.

Sibling comparison: the nearest sibling is projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline (same recruiting domain). Shared concepts exist - one-stage moves, a per-vacancy capacity limit, per-job duplicate-email refusal, stale-revision refusal, atomic batch action, activity trail - but these are generic invariants of the domain, not renamed copies. Pellmoor's flows are interview panels and 1-5 scoring, versioned assessments invalidated by panel changes, offer/hired opening reservations, d3 funnel derived from stage history with loss attribution, and actor-scoped retry receipts (hiring-rules.md lines 1-60; criteria such as panel_change_invalidates_entire_assessment, exact_derived_funnel, receipt_identity_is_person_scoped_and_session_independent). HireOps has none of those; instead it has candidate sign-in and candidate-safe views, conversations with paging/unread/seen/drafts, live board sync without disturbing work, manual ordering, and undo - none of which appear in Pellmoor (grep for conversation/unread/draft/bulk/candidate sign-in in Pellmoor instruction and notes: only an unrelated 'undo that release' phrase at hiring-rules.md:66). Criterion id sets share no ids and differ in structure. Pellmoor's capacity is offer/hired openings, HireOps's is Interview places; Pellmoor allows only the hiring manager to move, HireOps lets recruiters move anything and managers only late stages. The other messaging sibling, threadline-chat, is a Slack-style channel/thread/reaction workspace; its instruction has no drafts, scroll anchoring or seen receipts, and no pipeline. So the task is not a nouns-swapped clone of either.

Domain plan: no written suite domain plan was found in the workspace (grep of NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md, TASK_AUTHORING_WORKFLOW.md, qc/README.md). Against the observable suite (37 project folders spanning marketplace, insurance, billing, editors, games, canvas, permits, repair, chat, recruiting), a recruiting operations slice fits; arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations' is distinct from every sibling slice, though it omits the 'full-stack-node-express-sqlite-' prefix most siblings use - a naming-convention observation, not a distinctness defect. Provenance line ('Adapted from the supplied HireOps task ... with an authored reference implementation and browser rubric') is honest about origin.

Adversarial tries: (a) a clone test - swapping Pellmoor's nouns (vacancy->job, opening->interview place) would still leave the panels/assessment/funnel/receipt criteria with nothing in HireOps to grade and HireOps's conversation/candidate/live/undo criteria uncovered, so a renamed Pellmoor would fail most hro_* criteria; (b) conversely a HireOps-conforming app would not satisfy Pellmoor's rubric. Distinctness therefore holds in both directions. This row is a static judgement; no runtime evidence is required for it.
